official.description: The Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship allows researchers to pursue their own work in applied monetary economics, macroeconomics and public finance within the international and multidisciplinary community at NIAS, and to meet Dutch academics, policymakers and representatives of financial institutions. It is funded by the Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship Foundation, established in 2007 and supported by De Nederlandsche Bank, the Dutch Ministry of Finance, ING Group, Rabobank, ABN AMRO and AEGON.
official.program_type: Fellowship in economics at a national advanced study institute, funded by the Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship Foundation
official.english_requirement: Applicants should speak and write English well enough to take a full part in the life of the institute and to benefit from the responses of their peers; no test score is specified

applicant_utility.summary: Only one of these fellowships exists per academic year, and the Foundation states it prioritises an outstanding record in its three core fields, so this is a senior-researcher award rather than an early-career grant, even though early-career applicants are technically welcome. The proposal has to do something unusual for NIAS: it must argue that your work improves by being argued with by historians, sociologists and literary scholars, and that you will contribute back to that mixed room in return. Because the call is only two months long and the next round funds the 2028-2029 academic year, the practical preparation time is short and the ten-month option is worth considering if your project is long.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Established monetary or public-finance economists and policymakers, at least three years past the PhD, with a strong publication record and a project that gains from five or ten months of interdisciplinary debate in Amsterdam.
application_readiness_checklist: Decide between the five-month and ten-month option before drafting, since the proposal length and scope should match the period you request
Build the case for interdisciplinary engagement explicitly, naming the kind of NIAS colleagues and disciplines your question would benefit from
Keep the proposal within 1,500 words including footnotes and excluding references, and make sure the CV reflects your current position and recent output
If you are affiliated with a Dutch institution, settle the funding route early, since a Dutch University Grant is paid to your institution rather than to you
Confirm the four-days-a-week presence in Amsterdam is compatible with teaching, committee or policy duties before committing
common_rejection_risks: A technically excellent but narrow macroeconomics proposal that does not engage with the multidisciplinary NIAS community
Applying early in the career when the Foundation's stated priority is an outstanding record in applied monetary economics, macroeconomics or public finance
Exceeding the 1,500-word proposal limit, which includes footnotes
Requesting the ten-month award for a project that only needs five months, which reads poorly against a single annual fellowship
Overlooking that policymakers as well as researchers are eligible, and therefore not articulating the policy relevance of the work
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Flights, most living costs and relocation to Amsterdam are not covered; the award is a stipend or a grant to your home institution, with accommodation only subsidised where eligible and local public transport reimbursement as the fallback.
document_audit: Only three parts make up the application, so the proposal and CV carry the entire case and there is no room for a covering letter
The CV must be up to date, not a standard academic CV updated once a year, since it is read against an outstanding-record criterion
Reflect in the proposal on benefit from and contribution to NIAS, not only on your own research plan, because that is what the Foundation asks for
The proposal word count excludes references but includes footnotes, so move material into references rather than footnotes if you are near the limit
alerts: The next call funds the 2028-2029 academic year even though it closes in March 2027, so the gap between application and fellowship is long and plans must be stable
The call window is only two months, from 15 January to 15 March at noon CET
Until 2022 the fellowship was awarded by invitation only and it has been open to application since 2023, so it is a young and still unfamiliar process
NIAS publishes no euro amount, so do your financial planning against a stipend of unknown size and confirm expectations with NIAS before accepting
The Foundation has no employees and NIAS provides the administrative support, so practical questions should go to NIAS rather than to the Foundation
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One online form with a proposal and CV upload during the 15 January to 15 March call window, then ranking by the Duisenberg Fellowship Foundation's priorities with NIAS advising on cohort fit, and a single award per academic year.
